title: Iran - On a Collision Course
summary:
Iran - On a Collision Course
The United Nations Security Council may take up the issue of trade sanctions against Iran depending on developments related to their nuclear intentions. If this occurs, Iran is threatening to curb its oil exports. This issue has oil markets nervous (but not tanker markets just yet) as Iran is a large source of crude oil exports.

children.title: Iranian
children.summary: Revolution In summary: 2 2.4 million bpd of Iran's 4.1 million bpd, or 60% of its production, comes from six oil fields that have been in production individually for 40 to 70 years; 2 Well passed their peak production, annual output from these fields is falling of the order of 240,000 - 300,000 per year; 2 Near term projects will compensate for this decline increasing overall Iranian production of the order of 50,000 bpd per year; 2 Iranian domestic oil consumption is growing rapidly as a result of low product prices; 2 The net result is a slow decline in export availability, or at best level exports; 2 Iran's expressed desire to increase production to 5.8 million bpd in 5 years needs to attract $70 billion in investments; 2 Several projects are experiencing delays from difficulties in getting government approvals; 2 The new government has not provided any indication of wanting to attract either foreign capital or technology to develop its oil and gas resources. Can The World Survive Without Iran?
